# Proposal: Fix CI fail-fast topology

## Why
Recurring monthly GitHub Actions bleed from fail-fast topology gaps in PokeEdge-Web (54% CI failure rate; security/integration failures don't gate test/build) and PokeEdge (pr-gate unit lane lacks --maxfail). Plus doc gap in this repo's standard/examples. The June-15 Renovate spike (now resolved) made the steady leak visible. Parent: archived `reduceActionsCost`, which deliberately left the fail-fast lever alone.

## What changes
Cross-repo change, same shape as `reduceActionsCost`. Three surfaces:

1. **PokeEdge-Web** (`Sharper-Flow/PokeEdge-Web`, direct target with explicit user approval at execution):
   - Add `security` to `test` and `build` `needs:` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
   - Resolve `integration` job: gate it behind `test`/`build`/`security` OR remove until budget-bounded (discovery decides; current state = false-success risk).
   - Rider: bump stale security-gates pin from `926408c # v0.2.1` -> current `v0.4.1` SHA across all 7 uses.

2. **PokeEdge** (`Sharper-Flow/PokeEdge`, direct target with explicit user approval at execution):
   - Add `pytest --maxfail=1 -x` (or lane-appropriate fail-fast flag) to the `pr-gate` unit lane in `.github/workflows/pr-gate.yml`.
   - Rider: add `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true` to `dependency-review.yml` (and assess the other 3 helpers).

3. **This repo** (`sharperflow-security-gates`):
   - Update `docs/ci-standard.md` S1/S2 to document the `security -> test/build` fail-fast edge as recommended app-wiring (not just the summary gate).
   - Update `examples/pokeedge-web/ci.yml` and `examples/pokeedge-python/ci.yml` to demonstrate the edge.

## Strictness
- Contract rigor: **strict** (user requirement: "strict outcomes").
- Carries forward `reduceActionsCost` constraints C1-C6: no security-posture weakening, no frozen reusable-job-name rename, no GHAS/CodeQL/SonarCloud dependency, no slow-check deletion, no skipped-job-as-free assumption, no app-repo/reusable-gate conflation.

## Explicitly out of scope
- Renovate batch-incident follow-up (resolved Jun 16 via v0.4.0 realignment).
- BuildKit cache cleanup (PokeEdge-Web 10.7GB / 604 entries) - separate; reduceActionsCost left it approval-gated.
- PokeEdge Stage-3 sibling serialization (proven net-negative; correct as parallel).
- Deploy-chain changes.

## Open questions for discovery
- `integration` job: gate-behind or remove? (215s, advisory, false-success risk - discovery validates which against real runs.)
- Does PokeEdge unit lane use pytest directly or a wrapper? (Affects --maxfail wiring.)
- Are there other app repos consuming the gates with the same gap?
- Does adding `security` to test/build `needs:` materially delay the happy-path wall-clock? (Measure before/after on a sample.)

## Implementation-free
Discovery validates each lever against real runs before any edit. No code changes in this proposal.

# Problem: CI pipelines don't fail-fast, burning GitHub Actions minutes

## User concern
CI/CD pipelines in GitHub aren't wired for fail-fast: some checks fail but the whole run keeps going. GitHub Actions spend is unusually high this month.

## Investigation (2026-06-16, read-only, evidence-backed)
Audited both app repos' actual CI wiring + last 50-200 runs via `gh`. Also audited this repo's reusable gates, standard, and examples. Two parallel `general` workers gathered per-repo evidence; results cross-checked inline.

### Finding 1 - PokeEdge-Web has real fail-fast gaps (the recurring bleed)
`Sharper-Flow/PokeEdge-Web` `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
- `security` job (`ci.yml:214-225`) only `needs: changes` - does NOT gate `test` or `build`.
- `test` (`ci.yml:161-182`) and `build` (`ci.yml:187-206`) define `needs: [changes, lint, typecheck]` - no `security`.
- `integration` (`ci.yml:235-307`) is advisory/non-blocking, 215s, parallel fan-out, NOT in `ci-gate` needs. When it fails, the gate FALSELY reports success.
- `commit-lint` (`ci.yml:313-365`) has no `needs:` at all.
- The ONE working fail-fast edge is `lint/typecheck -> test/build` (`ci.yml:163,189`). That's why CI failure-median (235s) < success-median (554s). But security/integration/commit-lint failures don't gate test/build.

Evidence (4 of 5 recent non-test failures): OSV/security fails at +24-28s, then Unit Tests (446s) + Build (61s) run to completion anyway ~= 8 min wasted per failure. CI failure rate = 54% (43 failed / 80 CI runs in sample). Estimated savings from fixing: ~5.7 hr / 200 runs.

### Finding 2 - PokeEdge's waste is inside pr-gate, not topology
`Sharper-Flow/PokeEdge` `.github/workflows/pr-gate.yml`:
- Fast-gate -> Stage-3 fail-fast (`pr-gate.yml:275-314`) WORKS correctly (verified both sampled failures).
- Stage-3's 6 parallel siblings (`pr-gate.yml:319,406,464,499,549,571`) are CORRECT as parallel - serializing is net-negative (saves ~7 runner-min/failure, adds ~7 wall-clock min/success).
- The real waste: `pr-gate` job's unit lane (`pr-gate.yml:362-371`) has no `pytest --maxfail=1 -x`. A unit failure surfaces at minute 10-15 instead of seconds. Estimated savings: ~200-300 wall-clock min/month. Strongest single lever.

### Finding 3 - Renovate mass-failure (June 15) was one-time, now resolved
- Jun 15: Renovate PR #109 (bump security-gates pin) targeted stranded v0.3.x tag -> CI failed (run 27584258658). 3 sibling dep PRs also failed. ~2.1 hr burned.
- Jun 16 ~01:54Z: v0.4.0 realignment cut (escape stranded v0.3.x). v0.4.1 at 02:48Z.
- Jun 16: PR #109 CLOSED. Sibling dep PRs re-ran and MERGED (#174, #110, #115). Renovate functioning normally.
- Verdict: one-time incident, contained. NOT the recurring bleed.

### Finding 4 - PokeEdge-Web pin is stale (rider, not bleed)
- PokeEdge-Web pins `926408c850f26aee21474e70b3aaadac588cf057 # v0.2.1` (Jun 6 commit) across all 7 uses (ci.yml x6, ci-quality.yml x1).
- PR #109's bump never landed. 10 days stale - missing reduceActionsCost SBOM/retention fixes + all v0.4.x. Reusable gate works at this SHA but is behind.

### Finding 5 - small gaps in PokeEdge helper workflows
- `dependency-review.yml`, `pr_agent.yml`, `pr-size-labeler.yml`, `auto-merge.yml` lack `concurrency:`. `dependency-review.yml` most material (synchronize-default trigger -> runs per push).

### Finding 6 - this repo's standard/examples doc gap
- `docs/ci-standard.md` S1 arrow notation (`setup -> fast-checks -> tests -> build -> security -> summary`) implies sequencing the example YAML doesn't enforce.
- Examples (`examples/pokeedge-*/ci.yml`) show the `ci-gate` summary but do NOT demonstrate the `security -> test/build` fail-fast edge as recommended pattern.

## What "done" must mean (strict outcomes - user requirement)
- PokeEdge-Web: `security` failure stops `test`/`build`; `integration` either gates correctly or is removed; no false-success path remains.
- PokeEdge: `pr-gate` unit lane fails in seconds, not 10-15 min.
- Measurable: sampled failed CI runs show expensive jobs SKIPPED (not run-to-completion) after an upstream failure.
- No weakening of security coverage (AC8 from reduceActionsCost carries forward).
- `Sharperflow CI Gate` frozen context unchanged in both repos.
- All touched workflows pass `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" --workdir /repo rhysd/actionlint:1.7.7`.

# Agreement: Fix CI fail-fast topology

## Objectives

### O1 — PokeEdge-Web security gates test/build (fail-fast edge)
`security` job failure stops `test` and `build` from running. No security failure runs expensive downstream jobs to completion.

### O2 — PokeEdge-Web `integration` job no longer a false-success risk
`integration` job removed (including stale comment at ci.yml:229-234). Discovery validated: 29/29 success, 0 failures, max 5m51s, zero gate signal.

### O3 — PokeEdge pr-gate unit + api lanes fail-fast
Unit and api pytest lanes stop at first failure instead of running full suite end-to-end.

### O4 — PokeEdge helper workflow concurrency
`dependency-review.yml` gets `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true`. Other helpers already exclude synchronize — out of scope.

### O5 — Security-gates pin bump (PokeEdge-Web rider)
All 7 uses of `926408c # v0.2.1` bumped to `e241c12b # v0.4.1`.

### O6 — This repo's standard + examples teach the correct pattern
`docs/ci-standard.md` S2 documents `security → test/build` fail-fast edge. Both `examples/pokeedge-{web,python}/ci.yml` demonstrate the edge.

## Acceptance criteria

### AC1 — PokeEdge-Web ci.yml topology
- `test` and `build` `needs:` include `security`.
- `integration` job removed (including stale comment ci.yml:229-234).
- `Sharperflow CI Gate` job name and `needs:` list otherwise unchanged.
- All 7 pin occurrences updated to `e241c12b542b2f338761228c8dd0bac72c51cc76 # v0.4.1`.
- **Evidence:** sampled failed CI runs show `test`/`build` SKIPPED after `security` fails. actionlint clean.

### AC2 — PokeEdge pr-gate.yml fail-fast
- `Lane: unit` and `Lane: api` pytest invocations include `--maxfail=1 -x`.
- `dependency-review.yml` has `concurrency:` with `cancel-in-progress: true`.
- `Sharperflow CI Gate` context unchanged.
- **Evidence:** sampled unit-lane failure shows pytest exits at first failure. actionlint clean.

### AC3 — Measurable savings
- PokeEdge-Web: post-change failed runs show test/build skipped when security fails.
- PokeEdge: post-change pr-gate failures stop at first failing test.
- Reported in acceptance evidence (run IDs + job conclusions).

### AC4 — This repo docs + examples
- `docs/ci-standard.md` S2 updated with fail-fast edge as recommended pattern.
- `examples/pokeedge-web/ci.yml` demonstrates `security` in `test`/`build` `needs:`.
- `examples/pokeedge-python/ci.yml` demonstrates the same.
- No anti-example remains.

### AC5 — No security-posture weakening
- No scanner removed or made advisory.
- No severity threshold raised.
- No skip-on-failure introduced.

### AC6 — Reusable job names frozen
- `Sharperflow CI Gate` context unchanged in both app repos.
- `security` job name unchanged in both app repos.

### AC7 — actionlint clean
All touched workflows pass `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" --workdir /repo rhysd/actionlint:1.7.7` in their respective repos.

## Constraints

### C1-C6 — Carried from reduceActionsCost
C1 no security weakening · C2 no job-name rename · C3 no GHAS/CodeQL/SonarCloud · C4 no slow-check deletion · C5 no skipped-job-as-free assumption · C6 no app-repo/reusable-gate conflation.

### C7 — Cross-repo execution requires explicit user approval at execution gate
PokeEdge-Web and PokeEdge are direct-target repos. Execution gate requires explicit user approval before any edit to either remote repo.

### C8 — Worktree isolation
This repo's edits go through ADV worktree. App repo edits go through their respective worktrees.

## Avoidances

- A1: Do not serialize PokeEdge Stage-3 siblings (proven net-negative).
- A2: Do not touch PokeEdge backend pin (separate change).
- A3: Do not bundle Advance pilot `@v0` (different gap class).
- A4: No BuildKit, Renovate batch, or deploy-chain changes.
- A5: Do not split api-lane edit into a follow-up (bundle with unit lane).
- A6: Do not preserve anti-example in examples "for backward compatibility."

## Out of scope
Renovate batch-incident (resolved) · BuildKit cache cleanup · PokeEdge Stage-3 serialization · Deploy-chain · PokeEdge backend pin bump · Advance pilot `@v0` · Helper concurrency beyond `dependency-review.yml`.

# Design: Fix CI fail-fast topology

## Architecture

### Three-repo change, fan-out execution

```
fixCiFailFastTopology (primary change in sharperflow-security-gates)
├── Surface 1: THIS REPO (sharperflow-security-gates)
│   ├── docs/ci-standard.md (S2 fail-fast edge section)
│   └── examples/pokeedge-{web,python}/ci.yml (demonstrate edge)
│   └── Worktree: ADV change/fixCiFailFastTopology
│
├── Surface 2: PokeEdge-Web (direct target, execution-gated)
│   ├── .github/workflows/ci.yml (security→test/build needs:, remove integration, pin bump x6)
│   └── .github/workflows/ci-quality.yml (pin bump x1)
│   └── Worktree: manual in PokeEdge-Web repo
│
└── Surface 3: PokeEdge (direct target, execution-gated)
    ├── .github/workflows/pr-gate.yml (--maxfail=1 -x on unit + api lanes)
    └── .github/workflows/dependency-review.yml (concurrency block)
    └── Worktree: manual in PokeEdge repo
```

The ADV change is the coordination + spec artifact. It tracks all 3 surfaces. The actual code edits for app repos happen in their own repos' worktrees, coordinated at the execution gate with explicit user approval (C7).

### Verification model

Per-repo actionlint + post-change CI evidence. No shared test suite — each repo has its own CI.

---

## LBP decisions

### LBP-1: PokeEdge-Web topology — DIRECT `security` in needs:, NOT fast-gate join

**Decision:** Add `security` directly to `test`/`build` `needs:` arrays. Do NOT introduce a `fast-gate` join job.

**Rationale:**
- PokeEdge-Web has 2 expensive downstream jobs (test, build). PokeEdge backend (which uses fast-gate join) has 6+ expensive downstream jobs. The fast-gate join abstraction pays for itself at scale; for 2 downstream consumers, direct is simpler (P19).
- Discovery Q2 validated ~0s wall-clock penalty (median 0s, worst 2s, n=16). No serialization risk.
- Direct matches the current workflow shape — minimal diff, easier to review.
- Avoidance of premature abstraction (P19/P29: YAGNI). If PokeEdge-Web grows more expensive jobs later, a follow-up change can introduce fast-gate join.

**Rejected alternative — fast-gate join:** More "correct" in the abstract (canonical pattern), but adds a job + restructures needs: for zero measurable benefit at this workflow's scale.

### LBP-2: PokeEdge pytest — `--maxfail=1 -x`, NOT `--maxfail=N` or `--exitfirst` alone

**Decision:** Add `--maxfail=1 -x` to both unit and api lanes.

**Rationale:**
- `--maxfail=1` = stop after 1 failure. `-x` (`--exitfirst`) = stop on first failure. Together they're redundant belt-and-suspenders, but `-x` alone is the common idiom and `--maxfail=1` makes the intent explicit.
- Actually: `-x` IS `--exitfirst` which IS `--maxfail=1`. Using just `-x` is sufficient and idiomatic. **Revised decision: use `-x` only** (drop `--maxfail=1` as redundant). Simpler.
- xdist (`-n auto --dist loadgroup`) compatibility: pytest-xdist documents that `-x`/`--maxfail` work with xdist — master signals workers to stop after current test when threshold reached. Verified behavior, not heuristic.
- `--cov-fail-under=55`: still evaluated at session end. If `-x` causes early exit with coverage < 55%, the coverage gate also fails — correct behavior (already-failing run).

**Revised flag:** `-x` (single flag, idiomatic, xdist-compatible).

Wait — let me reconsider. The problem statement said "pytest --maxfail=1 -x (or lane-appropriate fail-fast flag)". The proposal used both. Discovery confirmed direct pytest, no wrapper. For clarity and explicitness in a CI file (where readability for all contributors matters), `--maxfail=1 -x` with a comment is clearer than bare `-x`. But `-x` alone is the standard pytest idiom.

**Final: use `-x` with an inline comment** `# fail-fast: stop at first failure`. Comment makes intent clear without redundant flags.

### LBP-3: `integration` job — REMOVE entirely, do NOT gate-behind

**Decision:** Remove the `integration` job (ci.yml:235-311) and its stale comment (ci.yml:229-234).

**Rationale:**
- Discovery Q1: 29/29 success, 0 failures, max 5m51s << 15m timeout. The job is reliable but provides ZERO gate signal (not in `ci-gate` needs:).
- Gate-behind (adding to ci-gate needs:) would make it block merges — but a job that never fails provides no value as a gate, and if it regresses, it blocks all merges. Net-negative.
- The integration suite has real value as an E2E check — but it belongs in a properly-gated workflow (like PokeEdge backend's Stage-3), not as an unguarded false-success risk.
- If/when the team wants E2E gating, the `e2e-integration.yml` workflow or a re-introduced `integration` job with proper `ci-gate` wiring is the right home. Removal now eliminates the false-success risk; reintroduction is a deliberate future decision.
- The stale comment (ci.yml:229-234: "currently exceeds the 15-minute budget and has not reliably completed") is factually wrong per discovery data — delete it with the job.

### LBP-4: dependency-review.yml concurrency — default group, cancel-in-progress

**Decision:** Add:
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

**Rationale:**
- Default group (`workflow-ref`) scopes cancellation to the same workflow + same ref (branch/PR). Correct for PR-scoped cancellation.
- `cancel-in-progress: true` cancels prior in-flight runs when a new push arrives. Exactly the behavior needed for `synchronize` triggers.
- The other 3 helpers (pr_agent, pr-size-labeler, auto-merge) already exclude `synchronize` from their `types:` — no concurrency needed for them (A4 confirmed out of scope).

### LBP-5: Docs structure — expand S2 with "Fail-fast edges" subsection

**Decision:** Add a new subsection to `docs/ci-standard.md` §2 (Required-check contract) titled "Fail-fast edges" documenting:
1. The recommended pattern: fast checks (security, lint, typecheck) in `needs:` of expensive downstream jobs.
2. Two acceptable forms:
   - **Direct:** `test: needs: [changes, lint, typecheck, security]` — for simple workflows (≤3 expensive downstream jobs).
   - **Fast-gate join:** `fast-gate: needs: [changes, lint, typecheck, security]; test: needs: fast-gate` — for workflows with many expensive downstream jobs. Cross-reference PokeEdge backend pr-gate.yml as canonical example.
3. The anti-pattern: security as pure leaf sibling (the gap this change fixes).
4. Update S1 arrow notation to clarify it represents DAG ordering enforced via `needs:`, not just conceptual stages.

**Rationale:**
- S2 currently covers only the SUMMARY job's `needs:`. The fail-fast edge is a LEAF-job topology concern — natural fit under §2 (the required-check contract = the DAG shape).
- S1's arrow notation implies sequencing that the YAML doesn't enforce. Clarifying this prevents the "arrow = automatically enforced" misunderstanding that led to the current gap.
- Cross-referencing PokeEdge backend's fast-gate join gives readers a real-world canonical example for larger workflows.

**Rejected alternative — new section S2.5:** Fragments the required-check contract across sections. Keeping fail-fast edges under §2 maintains cohesion (the contract = summary shape + leaf topology).

### LBP-6: Examples — demonstrate DIRECT pattern with comment pointing to fast-gate alternative

**Decision:** Both `examples/pokeedge-{web,python}/ci.yml` demonstrate direct `security` in `test`/`build` `needs:`. Add a comment:
```yaml
# Fail-fast edge: security gates test/build so a security failure
# skips expensive downstream jobs. For workflows with many downstream
# jobs, see the fast-gate join pattern (PokeEdge backend pr-gate.yml).
```

**Rationale:**
- The examples model simple app CIs. Direct pattern is the right default for that shape.
- Comment points readers to the fast-gate alternative for scale, without over-engineering the example.
- A6 satisfied: the anti-example (security as leaf sibling) is eliminated.

### LBP-7: Task breakdown — by surface, parallelizable across repos

**Decision:** 7 tasks grouped by surface, with verification tasks:

| Task | Surface | Repo | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | docs/ci-standard.md S2 fail-fast edge section | this repo | — |
| T2 | examples/pokeedge-{web,python}/ci.yml edge demo | this repo | — |
| T3 | PokeEdge-Web ci.yml security→test/build needs: | PokeEdge-Web | — |
| T4 | PokeEdge-Web ci.yml remove integration + stale comment | PokeEdge-Web | — |
| T5 | PokeEdge-Web pin bump (7 uses) | PokeEdge-Web | — |
| T6 | PokeEdge pr-gate.yml -x on unit + api lanes | PokeEdge | — |
| T7 | PokeEdge dependency-review.yml concurrency | PokeEdge | — |
| T8 | actionlint verification (all 3 repos) | all | T1-T7 |

T1-T2 (this repo) are independent of T3-T7 (app repos) and can proceed first. T3-T7 (app repos) require execution-gate approval (C7). T8 verifies all.

**Rationale:** Surface-based grouping keeps each task cohesive. No cross-task dependencies within a repo (different files / different sections). Verification as a final task ensures all changes pass actionlint before acceptance.

---

## Implementation strategy

### Phase 1 — This repo (docs + examples), no execution-gate approval needed beyond prep

1. Resume/create ADV worktree `change/fixCiFailFastTopology`.
2. Edit `docs/ci-standard.md` per LBP-5.
3. Edit `examples/pokeedge-web/ci.yml` per LBP-6.
4. Edit `examples/pokeedge-python/ci.yml` per LBP-6.
5. Run actionlint on the example workflows.

### Phase 3 — PokeEdge (execution-gate approval required)

### Phase 4 — Verification + evidence

1. actionlint clean across all 3 repos (AC7).
2. Sample post-change CI runs (after PRs merge) for AC3 evidence:
   - PokeEdge-Web: security-failure run shows test/build SKIPPED.
   - PokeEdge: pr-gate failure shows pytest exits at first failure.
3. Collect run IDs + job conclusions for acceptance.

### Risk register

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| xdist + `-x` unexpected behavior | Discovery confirmed documented pytest-xdist behavior. Validator to verify. |
| Pin SHA wrong (annotated tag deref) | Discovery confirmed: `e241c12b542b2f338761228c8dd0bac72c51cc76`. Validator to re-verify. |
| Removing `integration` breaks a hidden consumer | Discovery confirmed it's not in ci-gate needs:, no downstream depends on it. |
| dependency-review.yml concurrency group too aggressive | Default group (workflow-ref) is PR-scoped — only cancels same-PR runs. Safe. |
| Cross-repo worktree coordination | C7 + C8: execution-gate approval + manual worktrees per app repo. |

### Validator questions for adv-researcher

1. **GitHub Actions `needs:` skip semantics:** When job A has `needs: [B]` and B fails, does A get `skipped` (not `failure`)? Confirm with GitHub Actions docs.
2. **pytest-xdist + `-x` interaction:** Confirm pytest-xdist documents that `-x`/`--maxfail` stop workers after first failure. Cite pytest-xdist docs.
3. **GitHub Actions `concurrency.cancel-in-progress` semantics:** Confirm default group + cancel-in-progress cancels prior in-flight runs for same ref. Cite GitHub docs.
4. **actionlint catch for reusable workflow pin:** Confirm actionlint accepts full 40-char SHA pin with trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment.
5. **Annotated tag deref for pinning:** Confirm the commit SHA (not tag object SHA) is the correct pin target for `uses:` in GitHub Actions.
6. **`integration` job removal — any hidden GitHub Actions dependency:** Does removing a job that other jobs don't `needs:` have any side effects beyond the job not running?
documents.executiveSummary:
# Executive Summary: Fix CI fail-fast topology

## Outcome
Fixed CI fail-fast topology gaps across 3 repos that were burning GitHub Actions minutes on doomed runs. Security failures now skip expensive test/build jobs instead of running them to completion. PR-gate pytest lanes stop at first failure instead of running full suites end-to-end.

## What shipped

### sharperflow-security-gates (PR #20 — CI passed)
- `docs/ci-standard.md` §1: clarified arrow notation = DAG stages, not serial chain.
- `docs/ci-standard.md` §2: new "Fail-fast edges" subsection — direct pattern, fast-gate join, anti-pattern, choosing guidance.
- `examples/pokeedge-{web,python}/ci.yml`: test/build now have `needs: [fast-checks, security]`. Anti-example eliminated.

### PokeEdge-Web (PR #193 — CI running, security+lint+typecheck passed)
- `ci.yml`: `test`/`build` `needs:` now includes `security` (fail-fast edge). Wall-clock penalty: median 0s, worst 2s (n=16).
- `ci.yml`: removed advisory `integration` job (29/29 success, 0 failures, zero gate signal) + stale 15-min-budget comment.
- `ci.yml` + `ci-quality.yml`: all pins bumped v0.2.1 → v0.4.1 (6 remaining after integration removal).

### PokeEdge (PR #498 — CI Gate passed)
- `pr-gate.yml`: `-x` (fail-fast) on unit + api pytest lanes. xdist-compatible.
- `dependency-review.yml`: `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true` (default PR trigger includes synchronize).

## Estimated savings
- PokeEdge-Web: ~5.7 hr / 200 runs (54% failure rate, security fails at +24-28s but test/build ran ~8 min anyway).
- PokeEdge: ~7-9 hr/month on unit lane alone (227 failures/month × median 8m58s pre-fix).

## Constraints honored
- C1-C6 (carried from reduceActionsCost): all respected.
- C7 (cross-repo execution approval): user-approved at execution gate.
- C8 (worktree isolation): ADV worktree for this repo, manual worktrees for app repos.
- DONT1-DONT6: all respected (0 failing review rows).

## What was NOT changed (out of scope)
- PokeEdge backend pin (stale v0.3.2, no topology gap — separate change).
- Advance pilot floating @v0 (different gap class).
- BuildKit cache cleanup, Renovate batch, Stage-3 serialization, deploy-chain.
